rubrics.rubric: Does the submission provide both requested deliverables in usable text form?
criterion: The submission includes a clerk disposition and financial entry note in plain text.
The submission includes draft text for the 22nd Judicial District extended payment plan agreement.
The submission presents the two deliverables as distinct usable outputs rather than replacing them with process commentary.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note identify the correct case and defendant?
criterion: The note identifies the defendant as Jordan Ramirez.
The note identifies Citation No. 26TR-45871.
The note identifies Jefferson County Circuit Court, 22nd Judicial District, or an equivalent unmistakable court reference.
The note identifies the charge as ORS 811.109(5), speeding 102 mph in a 65 mph zone, or an equivalent description of the same violation.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note record the disposition accurately?
criterion: The note states that the court accepted a no contest plea.
The note gives the plea or disposition date as November 12, 2026.
The note does not describe any other charge, sanction, or collection referral as part of the disposition.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note use the correct standard fine from the statewide schedule?
criterion: The offense is treated as speeding 100 mph or greater under ORS 811.109(5).
The note states the standard fine as $1,150.
The note does not substitute a minimum or maximum amount such as $2,000 for the standard fine.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note apply the Jefferson County surcharge correctly?
criterion: The note includes a Jefferson County traffic surcharge of $5.
The surcharge is linked to Jefferson County rather than another county or a generic unsupported surcharge.
The note does not omit the surcharge.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note state the correct assessed starting balance?
criterion: The total amount due at disposition is stated as $1,155.
The total reflects $1,150 plus $5.
The note does not add a late-payment fee, collection charge, or any other unsupported amount to the assessed starting balance.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note record the court-approved payment plan terms accurately?
criterion: The note states a recurring monthly payment of $50.
The note states the first payment date as December 15, 2026.
The note states that the extended payment plan agreement was entered after disposition.

rubrics.rubric: Does the clerk note calculate the installment schedule correctly?
criterion: The note states that there are 23 full $50 installments.
The note states that the final smaller payment is $5.
The installment description resolves the full $1,155 balance rather than leaving a remainder or overstating the total.

rubrics.rubric: Is the clerk note written as a case-management entry rather than as an essay or instructions to another person?
criterion: The note is plain text.
The note combines the disposition and financial facts into a usable record entry.
The note avoids placeholder prose, speculative advice, or long-form narrative that would not belong in the case management record.

rubrics.rubric: Does the payment-plan draft use wording and field labels that fit the attached 22nd Judicial District form?
criterion: The draft includes a case or account reference field such as `Case # / Account #` or an equivalent local-form label.
The draft includes a balance field such as `Case/Account Balance`.
The draft includes an `Action Table(s) / Notes` field or equivalent clerk-notes section.
The draft includes a `TERMS of PAYMENT` line or equivalent monthly-payment clause suitable for the local form.

rubrics.rubric: Does the payment-plan draft populate the identifying fields correctly?
criterion: The debtor or defendant is identified as Jordan Ramirez.
Citation No. 26TR-45871 is used as the case or account reference if no separate case number is supplied.
The draft clearly ties the agreement to this single Jefferson County traffic matter.

rubrics.rubric: Does the payment-plan draft state the correct balance and payment terms?
criterion: The case or account balance is stated as $1,155.
The terms state $50 per month beginning December 15, 2026.
The payment clause states that payments continue until paid in full or modified, or uses an equivalent form-consistent completion phrase.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Action Table(s) / Notes text give concise clerk-review information that matches the case?
criterion: The notes identify the violation as ORS 811.109(5) or speeding 100 mph or greater.
The notes identify the disposition date as November 12, 2026 and the plea as no contest, or state an equivalent accurate disposition summary.
The notes identify the assessed balance basis as the standard fine plus Jefferson County surcharge, or provide an equally clear equivalent summary.

rubrics.rubric: Does the payment-plan draft avoid adding unsupported amounts to the starting balance?
criterion: The draft does not pre-add an ORS 1.202 late-payment fee or any other statewide payment-plan fee into the stated case balance.
The draft does not treat a collection fee, DMV fee, or returned-check fee as already imposed in this case.
The draft does not add any other charge, sanction, or collection referral that the assignment says is not part of this matter.

rubrics.rubric: If the draft includes additional agreement warnings, are they faithful to the attached local form?
criterion: Any nonpayment consequences mentioned are consistent with the attached 22nd Judicial District payment-plan form or a faithful paraphrase of it.
The draft does not invent interest, autopay requirements, community service conversion, or other terms not reflected in the attached form.
The draft does not change the basic local-form payment context, such as who payments are payable to or the nature of the agreement.

rubrics.rubric: Are the clerk note and payment-plan draft internally consistent on the financial terms?
criterion: Both deliverables use the same balance of $1,155.
Both deliverables use the same recurring payment amount of $50 per month.
Both deliverables use the same first payment date of December 15, 2026.

rubrics.rubric: Does the submission preserve the post-disposition sequence of events?
criterion: The disposition occurs on November 12, 2026.
The payment plan is presented as approved after disposition rather than before the plea or as a pre-hearing release condition.
The first payment date of December 15, 2026 is treated as a later obligation, not as the disposition date.
